name: Non-syndromic Pansynostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Pansynostosis

criteria.description: Premature fusion of all cranial sutures confirmed by imaging
Lack of extracranial anomalies or syndromic features associated with craniosynostosis syndromes
Presence of abnormal cranial shape consistent with pansynostosis
Negative genetic testing for known syndromic craniosynostosis mutations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Premature fusion of all cranial sutures with characteristic cranial deformity and absence of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and clinical exclusion of syndromic causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Premature fusion of all cranial sutures
Abnormal cranial vault shape (brachycephaly or cloverleaf skull)

common.symptomName: Increased intracranial pressure signs (e.g., bulging fontanelle)
Developmental delay secondary to cranial constriction
searchTerms: slow growth due to brain compression

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances due to optic nerve compression
searchTerms: vision problems from optic nerve pressure
blurred vision due to nerve compression

occasional.symptomName: Seizures related to increased intracranial pressure
Sleep apnea due to craniofacial abnormalities
searchTerms: sleep apnea from facial bone problems
obstructive sleep apnea due to skull shape

occasional.symptomName: Hearing impairment secondary to cranial base abnormalities
searchTerms: hearing loss from skull base issues
impaired hearing due to cranial abnormalities
ear problems linked to skull shape

rare.symptomName: Cognitive impairment unrelated to intracranial pressure
searchTerms: learning difficulties not from brain pressure
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems
fluid buildup in brain needing shunting

imaging: CT scan showing premature fusion of all cranial sutures
MRI to assess intracranial pressure effects and brain morphology
genetic: Negative for mutations in FGFR2, FGFR3, TWIST1, and other syndromic craniosynostosis genes
other: Clinical examination revealing abnormal head shape and absence of syndromic features

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of extracranial anomalies such as limb abnormalities
Positive genetic mutations in FGFR or TWIST genes
Scaphocephalic head shape rather than brachycephalic

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (vomiting, irritability, bulging fontanelle)
references: Cohen MM Jr. Craniosynostosis: Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Management. 3rd ed. Oxford University Press; 2000.
Wilkie AO, Johnson D, Wall SA. Clinical genetics of craniosynostosis. Curr Opin Pediatr. 2017;29(6):622-628.
